definitions.explanation: For time or a point to pass by.
To go past a limit or boundary.
Attached to verb stems or adjective stems to mean 'too much' or 'excessively.'

examples.notes: Auxiliary usage: verb stem + すぎる

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{難|むずか}し→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧{過|す}ぎる。
⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{過|す}ぎて⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{気|き}がついた→気付く：01933_kizuku⟧。
examples.english: I noticed after I had passed the station.
examples.notes: Main verb usage: pass by a place

examples.japanese: ⟦{期限|きげん}→期限：12861_kigen⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{過|す}ぎた。
⟦{嵐|あらし}→嵐：01695_arashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{過|す}ぎ⟦{去|さ}った→去る：02115_saru⟧。
⟦{制限|せいげん}→制限：03375_seigen⟧⟦{速度|そくど}→速度：03319_sokudo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{過|す}ぎた。
⟦{予算|よさん}→予算：03663_yosan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{過|す}ぎて⟦しまった→仕舞う：03064_shimau⟧。
⟦{限度|げんど}→限度：00063_gendo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{過|す}ぎる。
⟦{定員|ていいん}→定員：04532_teiin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{過|す}ぎたので⟦{入|はい}れなかった→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: We couldn't get in because it exceeded capacity.

examples.japanese: ⟦{高|たか}→高い：00500_takai⟧{過|す}ぎて⟦{買|か}えない→買う：00489_kau⟧。

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: ⟦{自動詞|じどうし}→自動詞：10977_jidoushi⟧ (intransitive) as a main verb. Its transitive partner is ⟦{過|す}ごす→過ごす：02062_sugosu⟧ (to spend time). Compare ⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{過|す}ぎる (time passes, by itself) with ⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{過|す}ごす→過ごす：02062_sugosu⟧ (someone spends the time). Note that {過|す}ぎる itself takes を in the sense 'pass by a place' (⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{過|す}ぎる) — that を marks a route, not an object, so the verb is still intransitive.

ASPECT: ている gives a resulting state. {過|す}ぎて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ = 'has already passed', as of a deadline or an hour.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{過|す}ぎる: time passes
- ⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{過|す}ぎる: go past a station
- ⟦{期限|きげん}→期限：12861_kigen⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{過|す}ぎる: a deadline passes
- 〜{過|す}ぎる: the auxiliary use, below

AUXILIARY USE (very common):
Attached to a stem, {過|す}ぎる means 'too much'. It is normally written in hiragana as すぎる in this use, and it conjugates as an ordinary ichidan verb (すぎた, すぎて, すぎない).
- Verbs — masu-stem: ⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧すぎる (eat too much), ⟦{飲|の}み→飲む：00322_nomu⟧すぎる (drink too much)
- I-adjectives — drop the い: ⟦{高|たか}→高い：00500_takai⟧すぎる (too expensive), ⟦{大|おお}き→大きい：00335_ookii⟧すぎる (too big)
- Na-adjectives — attach to the stem: ⟦{静|しず}か→静か：00755_shizuka⟧すぎる (too quiet)
- Two irregulars worth memorising: ⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧ becomes よすぎる, and ⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ becomes なさすぎる

The auxiliary almost always carries criticism or worry — 'too much' in the sense of a problem, not simply 'very'. ⟦{高|たか}→高い：00500_takai⟧すぎる says the price is unacceptable, not merely high.

SIMILAR VERBS:
- ⟦{経|た}つ→経つ：09892_tatsu⟧: also 'time passes', but only of elapsed duration, never of passing a place or exceeding a limit
- ⟦{通|とお}り{過|す}ぎる→通り過ぎる：02372_toorisugiru⟧: pass by and keep going, with the passing itself in focus
